summary: The article argues that cybersecurity is essential to preventing internet service disruptions, citing outages since September 2023. It profiles cybersecurity professionals and two case studies (a DDoS attack on WebAccess and a ransomware attack on SecureFlow), and covers tools, collaboration, resilience and future threats from IoT, 5G and quantum computing.
one_line: Overview of how cybersecurity professionals, tools and collaboration prevent internet disruptions, with DDoS and ransomware case studies from late 2023.
key_facts: A spate of high-profile service outages has hampered businesses and consumers since September 2023.
Sarah Johnson of ProtectNet Inc. said in an October 12, 2023 interview that the work of cybersecurity professionals is 'largely unseen, but it makes all the difference.'

The Cybersecurity Analysis Group, co-founded by Dr. Emily Chang, released a report on November 5, 2023 on vulnerabilities in internet infrastructure, including ageing hardware, software flaws and increasingly complex attacks.
Dr. Emily Chang claimed about 350,000 new malicious programs and potentially unwanted applications appear each day.
On October 19, 2023, a DDoS attack hit WebAccess, a leading internet service provider, disrupting service for millions of users across the East Coast.
Alex Ramirez, a senior cybersecurity analyst at GuardLayers Tech, helped mitigate the WebAccess attack by identifying attack vectors and filtering out malicious traffic.

On September 22, 2023, a ransomware attack on SecureFlow, which provides critical infrastructure for several online retailers, encrypted its data and took checkout services offline for nearly 48 hours.
Chloe Martinez, head of cybersecurity at SecureFlow, said the company recovered its data without giving in to the ransom demands.
Defenders use firewalls, antivirus software, intrusion detection systems and machine learning algorithms to detect anomalies in network traffic.
Training and awareness programs are described as essential because sophisticated security systems can be undone by human error.
The Cyber Threat Alliance (CTA) and the Global Cyber Alliance (GCA) share threat intelligence and resources to strengthen collective defenses.
The focus is shifting toward cyber resilience: continuing to operate under duress and recovering quickly after incidents.
Lisa Zhou, a cybersecurity trainer, advocates 'a culture of security within organizations' and runs workshops and simulations.
IoT, 5G and quantum computing are expected to bring both new innovation opportunities and new vulnerabilities.
